name: @projexlight/sdk-data-rights
summary: Subject data-rights orchestrator for ProjexCloud (G5 closer): per-person pool-residency registry tracks every store any tenant SDK has ever touched for a subject, so DSAR / right-to-erasure / right-to-portability can fan out completely + verifiably. Request walks plan → executions → certificate. Reconciliation worker catches drift between the residency registry and reality. The compliance lever every GDPR / HIPAA / CCPA / LGPD tenant relies on.

endpoints.description: Internal: any SDK that writes data keyed by a subject calls this on first touch so the residency registry knows that store now holds data for the subject.
List every store registered as holding data for a person. Operator-visible.
Open a new data-rights request (access / erasure / portability / restriction).
Read request state + plan + execution results + signed certificate (when complete).
Operator-driven state transition (e.g. accepted → executing → reviewed → completed).
Materialize the execution plan from the residency registry: one execution row per store.
Per-store SDK reports its result (success + payload, or failure + reason).
Issue the signed completion certificate after reconciliation confirms every execution succeeded.
Trigger a reconciliation pass — compares residency registry vs. actual store membership, raises drift events.

events.name: data-rights.residency.touched.v1
events.description: Subject's residency registry updated; new store added.

events.name: data-rights.plan.materialized.v1
events.description: Execution plan generated from the residency registry.

events.name: data-rights.execution.completed.v1
events.description: Per-store execution reported success or failure.

events.name: data-rights.certificate.signed.v1
events.description: Final certificate signed; subject + auditors can verify.

events.name: data-rights.reconciliation.drift.v1
events.description: Reconciler found a store holding data the residency registry didn't know about. Investigated immediately.

models.description: (person_id, store_ref) tuples. The single canonical answer to 'where does this subject's data live?'.
Request row: subject, request_kind (access / erasure / portability / restriction), status, opened_at.
Per-store execution row: store_ref, owner_sdk, status, result_payload (encrypted), completed_at.
Completion certificate: request_id, signed_at, signing_chain_id, summary.

hooks.name: touchResidency
hooks.description: Universal — every SDK calls this on first subject-keyed write. Idempotent on (person_id, store_ref).

hooks.name: openRequest
hooks.description: Open a DSAR. Returns request_id immediately; planning happens async.

hooks.name: materializePlan
hooks.description: Walks the residency registry + creates execution rows per store. Each store's owning SDK is notified to execute.

hooks.name: reportExecutionResult
hooks.description: Per-store SDK reports back via this (sdk-billing reports billing rows, sdk-evidence reports evidence rows, etc).

hooks.name: signCertificate
hooks.description: Issued after every execution succeeds; signing chain attested by the regional chain-head key.

hooks.name: startReconciler
hooks.description: Background worker pass that catches drift between residency registry + reality.

scenarios.title: Every subject-keyed write registers residency
scenarios.when_to_use: Internal universal pattern. Whenever a SDK writes data keyed by a person_id, it calls touchResidency so the registry stays complete. Documented here so SDK authors know what to call.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Idempotent — same (person, store) pair counted once. Emits data-rights.residency.touched.v1 on the first touch. The DSAR plan-materializer now knows to include billing.invoice in any future request for this subject.

scenarios.title: Subject files an access request (GDPR Art-15)
scenarios.when_to_use: Customer's end-user requests a copy of every piece of data the customer holds about them.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Plan created with one execution per registered store. Each store's owning SDK runs its access query + reports payload back. Final certificate signs the bundle for download.

scenarios.title: Right-to-erasure — every store scrubbed + verified
scenarios.when_to_use: Subject revokes consent (sdk-consent fires the revoked event); this SDK consumes it + opens an erasure request automatically.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Request opened; plan materialized + per-store execution. Each owning SDK scrubs its data + reports back. Certificate signs the completion. The customer can prove the erasure to their regulator with the signed certificate.

scenarios.title: Reconciler finds an undeclared store
scenarios.when_to_use: Periodic check (default daily) that compares the residency registry vs. reality. Drift is rare but a Sev-2 — it means a SDK is writing subject data without touching the registry.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Drift event filed for human review. Tenant compliance officer sees the drift in the operator dashboard. Untouched SDK author must fix + backfill residency touches before next reconciler pass.

scenarios.title: Subject (or regulator) verifies the signed certificate
scenarios.when_to_use: Subject downloaded the access bundle months ago; needs to prove its integrity now.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Verification deterministic. Result either confirms the bundle is intact (good) or surfaces tamper evidence (Sev-1 incident).

compliance_posture.notes: The G5 person_pool_residency registry is the lever that makes GDPR Art-17 actually completable — without it, fan-out is best-effort. The reconciler is the integrity guarantee on that registry. Certificate signing chain provides the audit-grade proof regulators expect for an erasure attestation.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per request opened (DSAR + erasure free up to plan ceiling)
per certificate signed (one per completed request)
